title: bug(storage): bd-6cl LinearProjectSnapshotStore missing on Dolt server backend — pull-side Projects silently disabled
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Repro

bd 1.0.2 (44b324926) on houmanoids_www (which uses Dolt server backend, not embedded):

```
bd linear sync --pull --push --dry-run
Warning: Project pull failed: storage backend does not expose LinearProjectSnapshotStore
```

Pull-side Project handling is silently disabled. New Linear Projects created via UI won't be materialized as local epics. The bd-6cl feature ships effectively non-functional on the rig where it was supposed to be verified.

## Root cause

The bd-6cl P1+P2 commits implemented `LinearProjectSnapshotStore` on the embedded Dolt backend, but not on the regular Dolt-server backend (internal/storage/dolt/*). The engine's capability probe finds the interface unavailable and gracefully degrades the pull-side Project handling — except 'gracefully' here means 'silently broken on production rigs.'

bd-ajn's `LinearIssueSnapshotStore` (the sibling interface from the issue snapshot work) ships on BOTH backends — likely the right precedent. The engine's PullProjects path should work on either backend.

## Fix

Implement `LinearProjectSnapshotStore` on the Dolt-server backend at internal/storage/dolt/. Should be a straight port of the embedded Dolt impl (same CRUD pattern, same SQL — just the different connection / transaction model).

Migration 0036/0037 (linear_project_snapshots table) already runs against both Dolt server and embedded — that part is fine. Only the Go-side store implementation is missing.

While there: audit any OTHER capability-probe paths bd-6cl added that might have the same single-backend coverage gap. The capability-degrade pattern is good (engine doesn't crash) but it hides bugs like this when the missing impl is on the production-shape backend.

## Tests

- Build LinearProjectSnapshotStore on dolt-server backend with the same CRUD test shape as the embedded one
- Add an integration test that runs the bd-6cl pull-side path against the Dolt-server backend and asserts the warning does NOT fire + a baseline snapshot row IS written on first encounter

## Severity

P1: the bd-6cl feature shipped non-functional on the user's primary rig. The non-fatal warning is easy to miss; users would just see Linear-side Projects not materializing locally and have no idea why.

## Mayor's principle

This violates 'long-term correct fixes only.' Capability-degrade-to-no-op without a loud-failure mode IS a quick fix in disguise — it makes the build green at the cost of silent runtime breakage on real rigs.

For the fix PR, add a 'design intent' note: 'capability-degrade is acceptable for OPTIONAL features (e.g. label sync); REQUIRED features (e.g. Project pull when ProjectSyncer is configured) should hard-error instead of warn.' Then either downgrade Project pull to optional or hard-error this path.
close_reason: Fixed on feat/linear-snapshot-stores-dolt-server-backend (2 commits, ~640 LOC). P1+P2 ported both LinearIssueSnapshotStore and LinearProjectSnapshotStore to internal/storage/dolt/ (direct ports of the embeddeddolt impls). P3 added CRUD tests + a compile-time interface guard test that fails loudly if either impl regresses. P4 added checkRequiredStoreCapabilities hard-fail at Sync() entry per mayor's design principle — REQUIRED features (PostPullSnapshotter, ProjectPuller) now hard-error instead of warn when the matching store interface is missing. Codex 2 rounds: round 1 clean (2 nits addressed — error message anchor uses interface name as primary, bd reference archival; test comment overclaim fixed); round 2 clean (no blockers, confirmed all asserted substrings still match, confirmed HistoryViewer + tracker-side capabilities don't have same gap pattern). SCOPE NOTE: bd-ajn was ALSO silently broken on dolt-server backend (LinearIssueSnapshotStore missing); fixed as part of this work.

title: bug(linear): FetchIssueByIdentifier query missing parent + project field selections — reconciler idempotency broken
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Symptom

Both bd-9w3's parent reconciler AND bd-1ay's project membership reconciler produce false-positive "Would assign / Would set parent" lines for issues that ALREADY have the correct parentId / projectId set on Linear.

Verified on houmanoids_www after bd-go9 wet-run (which assigned all 61 descendants of hw-sv1v to the teleop-video-livekit Project): bd-1ay dry-run shows 61 "Would assign HOU-X to Project ..." lines — every single one already correctly assigned (mayor verified via direct Linear API).

Mayor caught this in bd-pcb's defer note:
> Parent reconciler showing 46 'Would set parent' mutations even though Linear already has them set correctly (verified HOU-166→HOU-202, HOU-180→HOU-205 via direct API). Possible idempotency-check failure in bd-9w3's reconciler.

## Root cause

`internal/linear/client.go::FetchIssueByIdentifier`'s GraphQL query does NOT select either `parent { id identifier }` OR `project { id }`. So Issue.Parent and Issue.Project come back nil from this code path even when Linear has them populated.

Both reconcilers use FetchIssueByIdentifier (via fetchIssueAcrossTeams) and check:
- parent_reconcile.go: `childE.issue.Parent != nil && childE.issue.Parent.ID == parentE.issue.ID` → ALWAYS false because Parent is nil
- project_reconcile.go: `issueE.issue.Project != nil && issueE.issue.Project.ID == link.ProjectID` → ALWAYS false because Project is nil

So idempotency-skip never fires; reconciler thinks every link needs mutation; wet-run would issue 100+ no-op API calls and bump every updatedAt unnecessarily (which would also tickle bd-ajn's content-mutation-overrides-status conflict on the next sync).

The bulk `issuesQuery` (used by FetchIssues/FetchIssuesSince) DOES select both fields correctly. Only the single-issue identifier-keyed fetch is broken.

## Fix

In `internal/linear/client.go::FetchIssueByIdentifier`'s query string, add two field selections inside the `nodes { ... }` block:

```graphql
parent {
    id
    identifier
}
project {
    id
}
```

Match the same shape used by issuesQuery (lines 87-90 already select parent in the bulk query; project is missing there too — should add for read-back parity per bd-cs1 round-2 follow-up).

## Tests

- Mock-server-based: TestFetchIssueByIdentifierPopulatesParentAndProject — assert that the parsed Issue.Parent and Issue.Project are populated when the mock returns them.
- Regression in parent_reconcile_test.go: TestReconcileParents_AlreadyAssigned uses a mock that includes parent in the response; assert Skipped==N (idempotent), not Updated==N.
- Same for project_reconcile_test.go.

## Why P1

User-visible impact: every dry-run after a clean migration shows 100+ false-positive "Would" lines. Wet-run would issue 100+ no-op API calls per sync. Tickles bd-ajn's conflict-resolution footgun on every sync after that. Currently blocks any clean post-bd-go9 sync.

## Provenance

Caught by mayor during bd-pcb verification (commit 6ab0a9012). Filed as separate per mayor's "file separately if confirmed" directive in bd-pcb's defer note. Confirmed by tracing the FetchIssueByIdentifier query in internal/linear/client.go.

## Defer
- The same bulk `issuesQuery` is missing `project { id }` selection too (bd-cs1 round-2 added `content` to projectsQuery but not `project` to issuesQuery). Same fix shape; include in this work or as a follow-up.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 63ae77aed on feat/linear-epic-project-syncer-engine-integrated. Added parent + project field selections to FetchIssueByIdentifier (single-issue) query, and project field to bulk issuesQuery (parent was already there). 3 regression tests pinning the query shape with tight regex. Verified on houmanoids_www rig: 'Would set parent' and 'Would assign to Project' false-positives went 46+61 → 0+0. Dry-run is now actionable — only genuine deltas remain. Codex 2 rounds clean.

title: bug(linear): bd-1ay doEpicSync ignores CreateClosed — closed top-level epics get Projects created on Linear
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Repro

bd 1.0.2 (6ab0a9012) on houmanoids_www:

```
bd linear sync --pull --push --dry-run
```

Shows 20 'Would create Project "X" for epic hw-Y' lines. Every one of those 20 epics is **closed** locally with all their children also closed (historical/abandoned work, not active). The user explicitly does NOT want Projects created for any of them.

## Root cause

`SyncOptions.CreateClosed bool` already exists in internal/tracker/types.go with the documented semantic:

> Default is false — closed beads without an external ref are skipped so ongoing syncs don't retroactively register completed local-only work.

This applies to non-epic beads via the existing doPush flow. **bd-1ay's doEpicSync was added without honoring CreateClosed.** It routes by external_ref shape (empty/Project/Issue/skip) but never checks epic.Status, so closed epics with empty external_ref hit the Create branch and get Projects created.

## Fix

In doEpicSync's per-epic routing, before any branch dispatch:

```go
if epic.Status == types.StatusClosed && (epic.ExternalRef == nil || *epic.ExternalRef == "") && !opts.CreateClosed {
    continue  // closed top-level epic with no Linear identity, skip per CreateClosed
}
```

This mirrors the existing CreateClosed gate on doPush. Same semantic, same default. Users who explicitly want historical Projects can pass --create-closed and accept the Linear noise.

Edge case to handle correctly: a closed epic that ALREADY has external_ref = Project URL (e.g. hw-sv1v after migration, were it to be closed later). Should still route to UpdateProject so MapEpicToProjectState propagates 'completed' status. The fix above already does this — the gate only kicks in when external_ref is empty.

## Tests

- Closed epic + empty external_ref + CreateClosed=false → skip, no API call
- Closed epic + empty external_ref + CreateClosed=true → CreateProject (existing behavior preserved)
- Closed epic + Project URL external_ref → UpdateProject regardless of CreateClosed (state propagation)
- Open epic + empty external_ref → CreateProject (existing behavior)

## Impact on user

Without this fix, the user cannot run a clean sync on houmanoids_www. The dry-run is unactionable because 20 of the planned mutations would create unwanted Projects. Workaround would be: close the existing local epics one-at-a-time, then per-epic scoped pushes — wildly impractical.

## Defer

- Parent reconciler showing 46 'Would set parent' mutations even though Linear already has them set correctly (verified HOU-166→HOU-202, HOU-180→HOU-205 via direct API). Possible idempotency-check failure in bd-9w3's reconciler. Likely independent of bd-1ay. File as separate bug if confirmed.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 0d202c957 on feat/linear-epic-project-syncer-engine-integrated. Added CreateClosed gate to doEpicSync's case extRef=='' branch, mirroring engine.go:863's existing gate for non-epic beads. Verified on houmanoids_www: dry-run 'Would create Project' lines went 20→0, hw-sv1v's Update path still fires correctly. 5 tests in engine_epic_sync_test.go (Dolt-Docker gated).

title: bug(linear): CreateProject sends full description, hits Linear 255-char limit
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Repro

bd 1.0.2 (fdaef876d) on houmanoids_www:

```
bd linear migrate-epic-to-project hw-sv1v
# plan output is correct (61 descendants enumerated)
# Error: migration failed: creating Linear Project for hw-sv1v: failed to create project: GraphQL errors: Argument Validation Error
```

No partial state — hw-sv1v.external_ref unchanged, no project created on Linear, no descendant assigned. Clean retry available once fixed.

## Root cause (verified via direct API)

Linear's `ProjectCreateInput.description` has a hard 255-char limit. Verified by replaying bd's exact payload through curl:

```
"userPresentableMessage": "description must be shorter than or equal to 255 characters."
"constraints": { "maxLength": "description must be shorter than or equal to 255 characters" }
```

hw-sv1v.Description is 840 chars. The same payload with a short description succeeds.

## Code site

`internal/linear/tracker.go:912` MapEpicToProjectState wrapper calls client.CreateProject(name=epic.Title, description=epic.Description, state).
`internal/linear/client.go:1287` sends `epic.Description` to ProjectCreate unchanged. No length check, no truncation, no overflow handling.

Same issue likely exists in UpdateProject — but only fires once Update is called with a new long description.

## Fix options

1. **Truncate description to 255, log truncation.** Simplest. Cuts on word boundary if possible. Linear shows the truncated description in compact views (e.g. project list); full text is lost.

2. **Truncate description, put full text in Project.content.** Linear Projects have a separate `content` field (rich body shown on project page) without the 255 limit. ProjectCreateInput accepts `content`. This preserves the full description while satisfying validation. Recommended.

3. **Hard refuse if description > 255 with a guidance message.** Pushes the problem back to the user; bad UX for legacy migrations where the bead description was authored before Linear was in the picture.

I'd ship #2 for the migration path. Use the bead's title-of-the-first-sentence (or first 200 chars + ' …') as the description; full text in content. The migration tool's plan-phase output should note the description-truncation behavior so users aren't surprised.

UpdateProject should follow the same pattern.

## Tests

- Regression: migrate-epic-to-project on a bead with description > 255 chars succeeds, Project created, content field contains full body, description is truncated.
- Boundary: description exactly 255 chars → no truncation, no content field needed.
- Empty: description empty → no content field, empty description OK.

## Retry plan after fix

Same dry-run plan should reproduce 61 descendants + 16 direct-sub-epic parentId clears + 1 hw-sv1v.17 skip warning. Then wet-execute reaches Project creation, this time succeeds.

## Codex catches to revisit

Pearl's E (multi-team refused at plan time) and D (close-state lookup moved to plan time) — please verify the new description-length check happens at PLAN time too, so the user sees the warning in --dry-run before the partial-run risk.
close_reason: Fixed via description/content split. CreateProject signature gains content param; both Create+Update truncate description to 255 chars (rune-counted, word-boundary preferred) and pass full text as content. UpdateProject clears stale content via nil when description shortens (codex round-1 E catch). Plan-time Note surfaces truncation in --dry-run. Verified on houmanoids_www: hw-sv1v dry-run prints 'Note: bead description (841 chars) exceeds Linear's Project description limit (255)...'. 12 unit-test sub-cases pass. Commit b3a05210d on feat/linear-epic-project-migration-integrated.

title: feat(linear): epic-identity migration tool — legacy Issue-backed top-level epics → Linear Projects
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Context

The epics-as-projects design (your bd-2og work, commits 6df45fe8b + 473528d28 + 9eff6aa6b) defines:

- **Top-level epic** (epic with no parent epic) → Linear **Project**
- **Sub-epic** (epic whose parent IS an epic) → Linear **Issue**, projectId = root Project, parentId = null (parent is the Project, not an Issue)
- **Sub-sub-epic / task** → Linear Issue, projectId = root Project, parentId = nearest parent Issue

Push correctly applies this for NEW top-level epics: doEpicSync creates Projects, doPush skips epics in epicProjectMap and uses projectId on descendants.

**But:** top-level epics that were created BEFORE the design landed have external_ref pointing at `/issue/HOU-N` (an Issue URL). doEpicSync currently treats external_ref as 'already synced' and never converts them. Result: they live in perpetuity as Issues, descendants nest via parentId rather than projectId membership, and Linear's Projects page never shows the work.

Concrete case on houmanoids_www:
- hw-sv1v (epic, root, 'teleop-video-livekit') → external_ref = `linear.app/houmanoids/issue/HOU-159` (Issue, not Project)
- 8 sub-epics (hw-sv1v.1..9) live as Issues HOU-158, HOU-202..209
- ~50 tasks live as Issues with parentId set (after the bd-9w3 reconciler fix), but no projectId

After bd-9w3 lands, the Issue tree will be nested correctly. But the conceptual / Project-page realization of the design is missing.

## Ask

Build a migration command — `bd linear migrate-epic-to-project <bead-id> [--dry-run]` — that, given a top-level epic with a legacy Issue-backed external_ref:

1. **Plan phase** (always runs, dry-run prints + exits):
   - Verify the bead is an epic with no parent-epic dep (refuse otherwise)
   - Verify external_ref is currently an Issue URL (refuse if already a Project URL — idempotency)
   - Enumerate all descendants via the same walk the parent reconciler uses (parent-child deps, transitively closed)
   - Print a preview: 'Would create Project "<title>" in team <id>; would set projectId on N issues; would close legacy Issue HOU-X with link to new Project; would update bead external_ref to <new project URL>'

2. **Execute phase** (when not dry-run):
   a. **Create the Project** on Linear via existing CreateProject (reuse the ProjectSyncer impl). Capture project URL + ID.
   b. **Set projectId on every descendant Issue** via Linear API. Batch if Linear's bulk update supports it; otherwise sequential with rate-limit awareness (use the same circuit breaker bd-ena added).
   c. **Update each descendant bead's external_ref?** No — descendants' Linear identities don't change; they're still the same Issues. Only the projectId changes.
   d. **Handle the legacy root Issue (HOU-159).** Options for user via flag:
      - `--legacy-issue=close` (default): close the Issue with a comment 'Migrated to Project <url>'. Set its status to closed/done.
      - `--legacy-issue=keep`: leave it open. Add a comment linking to the Project. (Useful if the user wants to keep the Issue as a permanent tracking marker.)
      - `--legacy-issue=delete`: delete the Issue from Linear (irrevocable; warn loudly).
   e. **Update the bead's external_ref** to point at the new Project URL.
   f. **Clear parentId** on direct-child sub-epics (hw-sv1v.1..9). Per design, sub-epics under a Project have parentId=null. Currently after bd-9w3 those would be parentId=HOU-159; after this migration HOU-159 either no longer exists or is no longer the parent. NOTE: this conflicts with the reconciler's behavior of always setting parentId. The migration needs to either (i) skip setting parentId in this case, or (ii) the reconciler needs to learn 'if parent epic was migrated to Project, set projectId on the child instead of parentId.'

3. **Tests:**
   - Happy path: legacy Issue → Project with full descendant migration
   - Idempotency: re-running on an already-migrated epic is a no-op
   - Partial failure: Project created but descendants partially updated → re-run should pick up where it left off (use the new Project's ID to detect which descendants still need projectId)
   - Refusal: refuse on non-epic / non-top-level / already-Project beads

## Reconciler interplay

The bd-9w3 fix you just shipped (parent reconciler) needs to learn the new rule:

- If a child's bead-side parent has external_ref pointing to a Project URL (IsProjectRef), set projectId on the child, not parentId
- For non-Project parents (Issues), keep current behavior (set parentId)

Add this as part of this work or as a separate follow-up — your call.

## Why not a config flag instead of a tool?

The migration is destructive (legacy Issue is closed/retired, external_ref rewritten). It can't safely run on every sync; needs a user-initiated invocation with a preview. Also Linear has no Issue→Project conversion API — this tool is fundamentally a 'create new + move children + retire old' workflow that doesn't fit inside a normal sync pass.

## Why now

Mayor explicitly chose to defer the houmanoids_www wet-sync until the full design is realized (rather than ship parent links half-done under HOU-159). Wet-sync is on hold until this lands. Other rigs without legacy Issue-backed top-level epics can already use the bd-9w3 reconciler fix.

## Scope confirmation needed from you

- How granular should the dry-run preview be? Per-descendant 'would set projectId on HOU-X' lines, or just a count? Mayor's preference: per-descendant, like the bd-5zh reconcile preview.
- Should the migration run as a single Dolt commit or in batches? Single commit means rollback-on-failure but bigger window.
- Multi-team: if descendants span teams, does each team need its own Project? (Probably not for our case — single team — but worth deciding.)
- Comments / attachments on HOU-159: do they migrate to the Project (Projects DO support comments) or stay on the legacy closed Issue?

Engage codex-rescue twice as before. Mayor available for design questions.
close_reason: Migration tool + reconciler skip shipped on feat/linear-epic-project-migration-integrated (commit fdaef876d). Mayor's spec wanted upstream branch but ProjectSyncer infrastructure only exists on the integration-sibling rooted side; ported as needed for v1. Verified end-to-end on houmanoids_www: dry-run produces 61 descendant assignments incl 13 direct-sub-epic parentId-clears + 1 unsynced warning for hw-sv1v.17. 17 unit-test sub-cases pass. Codex 2 rounds, 5 round-1 issues fixed (duplicate-Project, parentId clear semantics, loop idempotency, late state-map failure, multi-team routing), round-2 unsynced-warning gap fixed.

title: bug(linear): parent reconciler silently skipped all HOU-164..209 orphans on houmanoids_www despite null parents on Linear

On houmanoids_www rig with bd 1.0.2 (1dee1ce1f) — your integration sibling that shipped bd-5zh today.


1. **buildLinearParentLinks returns empty.** `store.SearchIssues(ctx, "", types.IssueFilter{})` may not be returning what you expect (e.g. only open + non-pinned, or missing the wisps merge), or `store` is nil at that call site, or the deps walk's `d.Issue.ID` access has wrong semantics — `IssueWithDependencyMetadata` embeds `Issue`, not `*Issue`; double-check the field name resolution.

3. **ReconcileParents fetchIssue returns issue.Parent populated even though Linear shows null.** If `Issue.Parent` is being constructed by bd from a cached snapshot or from a different field (e.g. `projectId` mistaken for parent), the idempotency-skip condition would mass-skip falsely.

4. **The integration sibling's bd-ena port misses something.** The composition commit (3cf4e857e) flagged that one test was omitted because bd-47l base lacks the rate-limit breaker; double-check no other call-site was lost in the cherry-pick (compare to upstream feat/linear-epic-parent-child).

- Identify whether the issue is in the link build, the fetch (issue.Parent population), or the idempotency-skip comparator.
- Fix + add a regression test that covers the null-Linear-parent / non-empty-local-link scenario. The existing DryRunNoMutations test apparently doesn't cover this real-world shape.

This is the exact orphan-repair use case bd-ena was built for (HOU-164..209). With the bug, dry-run shows clean, wet-run will also do nothing, and the orphan tree stays orphaned. The user (mayor) reasonably caught this by spot-checking Linear directly.

notes:
## Update from mayor: design context (epics-as-projects, March 2026)

Found the original design in commits **6df45fe8b** + **473528d28** (Mar 29 2026) and the consolidated **9eff6aa6b** (Apr 21 2026, ProjectSyncer interface at internal/tracker/tracker.go:174). The design intent:

- **Top-level epic** (epic with no parent epic) → Linear **Project** (NOT Issue)
- **Sub-epic** (epic whose parent IS an epic) → Linear **Issue** with parentId (regular issue hierarchy under the parent project)
- **Tasks under epics** → Linear Issue with both parentId (to nearest parent issue) AND projectId (to top-level project)
- doPush epic-skip path only skips epics that were synced as Projects (tracked in epicProjectMap)

## Why this matters for bd-9w3

The hw-sv1v tree on houmanoids_www is in a hybrid/legacy state:

- hw-sv1v has external_ref linear.app/houmanoids/issue/HOU-159 — Issue URL, NOT Project URL. So hw-sv1v was created as an Issue, not a Project. Pre-design legacy.
- hw-sv1v.1..9 are all Issues (HOU-158, HOU-202..209). Per design these CAN be Issues with parentId, but their Linear parent is null.
- hw-sv1v.X.Y tasks (HOU-164..201) are Issues with parentId=null.

## Hypothesis

Does buildLinearParentLinks or ReconcileParents have epic-aware filtering that silently skips links where the parent is type=epic? Look for any check like 'if parentIssue.IssueType == types.TypeEpic route to AssignIssueToProject instead' — if there is one, AssignIssueToProject would no-op because hw-sv1v isn't a Project on Linear, dropping the link without warning.

Even ignoring that, hw-sv1v.X.Y → hw-sv1v.X (sub-epic to sub-epic) should be unambiguous Issue→Issue parentId and should still produce mutations. There's a real bug regardless of the design-mismatch.

## What mayor needs

Two separable problems:

dispatched_by: mayor

# Revised Plan: Linear ↔ beads sync hardening + In Review preservation (v2)

## Goals

1. Stop bd sync from collapsing Linear's "In Review" state to "In Progress" when local bead fields change.
2. Preserve Linear's "In Review" as a state automatically driven by GitHub PR lifecycle.
3. Make the bd→Linear push resolver unambiguous so a future config drift can't silently flip closed beads to Canceled again.
4. Round-trip `deferred` correctly between beads and Linear.
5. Keep the existing IssueTracker interface contract intact for GitHub/Jira/ADO/Notion/GitLab.

## Non-goals

- Reshaping how cancellation is represented in Linear (we accept the loss of explicit Canceled state on the houmanoids team; close-reason lives on the beads side).
- Making bd's `close_reason` round-trip from Linear (no Linear payload field for it).
- Touching the reaper code (already fixed upstream at `internal/reaper/reaper.go:601`; current binary verified).

## Scope of changes

### A. bd code changes

**A1. Extend `ParseBeadsStatus` to accept `deferred`.**

File: `internal/types/types.go`
- Function: `ParseBeadsStatus` (around line 327)
- Add a `case "deferred": return StatusDeferred` clause alongside the existing cases.
- Audit any sibling status-string parsers in `types.go` (`Status.IsValid`, `IsValidWithCustom`) for completeness — `deferred` is already in the built-in switch in `IsValid` (line 339). Verify nothing else needs touching.

**A2. Add `StatusDeferred` to `StatusToLinearStateType`.**

File: `internal/linear/mapping.go`
- Function: `StatusToLinearStateType` (around line 394).
- Add `case types.StatusDeferred: return "backlog"` so a deferred bead pushed without explicit state map still resolves to a backlog-type Linear state via the type fallback.

**A3. Make `StateToBeadsStatus` prefer explicit name mappings over type mappings for the pull direction.**

File: `internal/linear/mapping.go`
- Function: `StateToBeadsStatus` (around line 290).
- Current behavior: type match first, then name match.
- New behavior: name match first (using `ExplicitStateMap`), then type match (using `StateMap`), then default. This lets `linear.state_map.deferred = deferred` win over the default `backlog → open` for Linear states named "Deferred".
- Important: do NOT regress existing behavior for teams that rely on type-only mapping. Testing must cover: (a) team with no explicit state_map.deferred — Backlog state still pulls as `open`; (b) team with explicit state_map.deferred — Deferred name-matched state pulls as `deferred`.

**A4. Add an optional secondary interface `UpdateIssueWithRemote`.**

Files: `internal/tracker/tracker.go`, `internal/tracker/engine.go`, `internal/linear/tracker.go`.

- In `internal/tracker/tracker.go` (around line 44, alongside the existing `IssueTracker` interface): add a NEW interface, e.g.:
  ```go
  // RemoteAwareUpdater is an optional capability. Trackers that implement it
  // receive the already-fetched remote payload so they can decide which fields
  // are safe to omit from the update (e.g., preserve states owned by external
  // automation).
  type RemoteAwareUpdater interface {
      UpdateIssueWithRemote(ctx context.Context, externalID string, issue *types.Issue, remote *TrackerIssue) (*TrackerIssue, error)
  }
  ```

- In `internal/tracker/engine.go` (the push update path around line 929–946 where `extIssue` is fetched and `UpdateIssue` is called): type-assert the tracker to `RemoteAwareUpdater`. If it implements it, call `UpdateIssueWithRemote(ctx, externalID, issue, extIssue)`. Otherwise fall back to the existing `UpdateIssue(ctx, externalID, issue)`. Do this in BOTH the conflict-local-force path (line 1046+) and the normal path. For force paths that currently skip remote fetch, fetch the remote first (one extra Linear API call per forced issue, acceptable).

- In `internal/linear/tracker.go` (around line 174 where `Tracker.UpdateIssue` lives): add a `Tracker.UpdateIssueWithRemote` method:
  ```go
  func (t *Tracker) UpdateIssueWithRemote(ctx context.Context, externalID string, issue *types.Issue, remote *tracker.TrackerIssue) (*tracker.TrackerIssue, error) {
      client := t.clientForExternalID(ctx, externalID)
      if client == nil { ... }

      mapper := t.FieldMapper()
      updates := mapper.IssueToTracker(issue)

      // Skip stateId when remote's mapped status already matches local —
      // preserves Linear-owned states like "In Review" driven by GitHub.
      if !t.remoteStatusMatchesLocal(remote, issue.Status) {
          stateID, err := t.findStateID(ctx, client, issue.Status)
          if err != nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("finding state for status %s: %w", issue.Status, err) }
          if stateID != "" { updates["stateId"] = stateID }
      }

      updated, err := client.UpdateIssue(ctx, externalID, updates)
      if err != nil { return nil, err }
      ti := linearToTrackerIssue(updated)
      return &ti, nil
  }
  ```
  
  Plus a helper `remoteStatusMatchesLocal(*tracker.TrackerIssue, types.Status) bool` that converts the generic remote back to the Linear `*State` via the existing field mapper, runs `StateToBeadsStatus`, and compares to local. If the conversion is lossy (the generic `TrackerIssue` doesn't carry the raw Linear state name/type), then have `UpdateIssueWithRemote` accept the raw Linear `*Issue` directly via a Linear-only path inside the engine — the engine has a fast-path for Linear because it already fetches via `client.FetchIssueByIdentifier`. Pick whichever is simpler.

  The existing `Tracker.UpdateIssue(ctx, externalID, issue)` stays as-is (no signature change), and internally calls `UpdateIssueWithRemote(ctx, externalID, issue, nil)` so the legacy code path doesn't regress for paths that don't have a remote on hand.

- Behavior when `remote == nil`: must NOT skip stateId. Falls through to the existing logic.

**A5. Remove or guard the unused `StateCache.FindStateForBeadsStatus` landmine.**

File: `internal/linear/client.go`
- Function: `FindStateForBeadsStatus` (around line 676–693).
- Choice: either delete it if no caller, or add a doc comment + deprecation notice pointing to `ResolveStateIDForBeadsStatus`. This function ignores explicit mappings and picks the first matching state by type — exactly the kind of footgun that produced the original Canceled regression.
- Verify no callers via `grep -r "FindStateForBeadsStatus" .` Codex's review flagged `cmd/bd/linear.go:377,380` and `engine.go:1327` as touching the surrounding plumbing — confirm none of them actually invoke it on a hot path.

**A6. Tests.**

Add to `internal/linear/mapping_test.go` and `internal/linear/tracker_test.go` (create if absent):

- `TestStateToBeadsStatus_ExplicitNameWinsOverTypeFallback` — explicit `linear.state_map.deferred = deferred` overrides default `backlog → open` for a Deferred-named backlog-typed state.
- `TestParseBeadsStatus_Deferred` — `ParseBeadsStatus("deferred")` returns `StatusDeferred`.
- `TestUpdateIssueWithRemote_PreservesInReviewOnTitleEdit` — bead status `in_progress`, remote Linear state "In Review" (type=started, name="In Review"), title differs → patch path runs, `updates` does NOT include `stateId`.
- `TestUpdateIssueWithRemote_PushesStateOnRealTransition` — bead status `closed`, remote Linear state "In Progress" → `updates` includes `stateId` resolving to Done.
- `TestUpdateIssueWithRemote_NilRemote_FallsBack` — `remote == nil` → behaves like legacy `UpdateIssue`, includes stateId.
- `TestEngineForcePushFetchesRemote` — verify the conflict-local force path still fetches remote so In Review preservation is honored.

Add to `cmd/bd/linear_roundtrip_test.go`:

- `TestRoundtrip_DeferredBackAndForth` — push deferred bead, pull, status remains `deferred`.
- `TestRoundtrip_PreservesInReviewAfterTitleEdit` — push bead title change, Linear state stays In Review.

### B. Pre-flight validation in `bd linear sync`

File: `cmd/bd/linear.go` (around line 214 where `ValidatePushStateMappings` is called).

- Extend the validator to require, for each beads status that has an explicit map entry, at least one matching Linear state on the team by either name or type (excluding `blocked` and `deferred` from the strict check OR including them). Choose: include them — i.e. if the rig config says `linear.state_map.blocked = blocked`, validation must confirm the team has a state named "Blocked". This catches "Phase 2 deployed before Phase 1" cleanly with a single error message instead of per-issue failures.
- Behavior: if validation fails, `bd linear sync` exits with a clear error before any push happens.
- Must be safe for trackers other than Linear (route only via the Linear tracker plumbing).
- Add test: `TestValidatePushStateMappings_FailsOnMissingDeferredState`.

### C. `bd linear sync --dry-run` accuracy

File: `internal/tracker/engine.go` (`doPush` around line 883–891).

- Currently dry-run prints "Would update" for every external-ref'd issue before fetching remote / applying ContentEqual. This doesn't reflect what wet-run actually does post-patch.
- Change: in dry-run, fetch remote and run the same equality check as wet-run before printing "Would update". For trackers implementing `RemoteAwareUpdater`, also simulate the stateId-skip decision by recomputing whether `updates` would actually include any non-equivalent fields.
- Output format: distinguish "Would push state change", "Would push field change (state preserved)", "Would skip (no diff)". Keeps the UX informative.
- Add test: `TestDryRunMatchesWetRunEqualityDecisions`.

### D. Linear-side reshape (UI work)

This is unchanged from v1, but resequenced after the bd patch deploys (D happens AFTER A–C).

D1. Connect Linear's GitHub integration (Settings → Integrations → GitHub) to `Houmanoids/houmanoids-www` and any other repos backed by HOU- issues.

D2. Configure auto-state-move rules:
   - PR opened referencing issue → state = "In Review"
   - PR merged → state = "Done"
   - PR closed without merge → revert to previous state

D3. Reshape team workflow:
   - Bulk-move issues out of **Canceled** and **Duplicate** to **Done** (or **Backlog**, per case-by-case judgment). Archive both states once empty. ACCEPTED LOSS: cancellation as a Linear state goes away; close-reason is recorded only in beads' `close_reason` column going forward.
   - Rename **Backlog** → **Deferred** (or add a new `Deferred` state, type=backlog, and migrate existing Backlog issues into it). Confirm the migration path doesn't re-trigger any auto-state rules.
   - Add **Blocked** state, type=started.
   - Keep **Todo**, **In Progress**, **In Review**, **Done** unchanged.
   - Final 6 states: Deferred, Todo, In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Done.

### E. bd config on the rig (after D)

```bash
cd ~/gt/houmanoids_www/mayor/rig
bd config set linear.state_map.deferred deferred
bd config set linear.state_map.todo open
bd config set "linear.state_map.in progress" in_progress
bd config set linear.state_map.blocked blocked
bd config set linear.state_map.done closed
# leave "in review" UNMAPPED so push never resolves to it
# linear.state_map.canceled was already removed
```

NOTE the explicit quoting on `"linear.state_map.in progress"` to handle the embedded space.

### F. Verification (Phase 4)

F1. `bd linear sync --dry-run` — expect no per-issue errors. Output should show 0 state changes for issues whose Linear state is "In Review" (because their bead is `in_progress` and remote-mapped status equals local).

F2. Open a test PR with `HOU-XX` in the title or body. Confirm Linear's GitHub integration moves the issue to "In Review".

F3. Run `bd linear sync` (real). Confirm the issue is STILL "In Review" afterward — not collapsed.

F4. Edit the bead's title locally. Run `bd linear sync`. Confirm Linear shows the new title AND state still "In Review".

F5. Merge the test PR. Confirm Linear moves to "Done". Run `bd linear sync`. Confirm bead becomes `closed` locally.

F6. Verify gt-side state writers do the right thing. Trigger each path on a small test bead (HOU-test-1, HOU-test-2, HOU-test-3) and verify Linear state after sync:
   - Refinery merge close (`gt/internal/refinery/manager.go:632,638`)
   - `gt done` force-close (`gt/internal/cmd/done.go:626,632`)
   - Witness reset of abandoned hooked beads (`gt/internal/witness/handlers.go:2048,2110`)

F7. Targeted: simulate a force/conflict push with In Review on remote. Confirm A4's force-path remote-fetch logic kicks in — Linear stays In Review.

## Sequencing (revised — patch first, then Linear reshape)

1. **A1, A2, A3 (status enum + mapping fixes)** — small, low risk.
2. **A6 tests for A1–A3** — must pass before A4.
3. **A4 (RemoteAwareUpdater interface + Linear tracker impl)** — biggest patch.
4. **A6 tests for A4** — must pass before merging.
5. **A5 (remove landmine)** — independent cleanup; do after A4.
6. **B (pre-flight validation)** — depends on A.
7. **C (dry-run accuracy)** — depends on A4 semantics.
8. **Build & install bd** — `make build && cp ./bd ~/go/bin/bd && codesign -s - -f ~/go/bin/bd`. Confirm with `bd --version`.
9. **Upstream PR for A–C** — non-blocking; can happen in parallel with rest.
10. **D (Linear reshape)** — only after patched bd is installed.
11. **E (rig config)** — must follow D, otherwise pre-flight will block sync.
12. **F (verification)** — full verification suite. If F1 fails, stop. If F3 or F4 fails, the patch is broken — revert and re-investigate.

## Rollback plan

- A revert is a clean revert of the bd patch + restore the unset `linear.state_map.canceled` IF Linear has been reshaped back to include Canceled. If Linear has been reshaped (D done), rollback also requires Linear-side restoration of Canceled and Duplicate states — non-trivial. So D is the point of no return.
- Recommend tagging the bd commit pre-patch as a checkpoint and snapshotting the rig's `bd config list | grep linear` output before D for restoration reference.

## Open questions

- Q1: Does Linear's `GraphQL Issue` payload include any field that proxies for "this is a cancellation" beyond the workflow state itself (e.g., a `cancelReason` field, or a label convention)? If yes, A4's helper should preserve it on round-trip and bd's `close_reason` could be populated from it. UNVERIFIED — needs Linear API docs check.
- Q2: Does the GitHub integration handle Linear → GitHub the other direction (e.g., closing the GitHub PR when issue is cancelled in Linear)? Not relevant to this plan but worth knowing for ops.
- Q3: Do we want to gate the bd patch behind a feature flag (`linear.preserve_remote_state = true`) to ease rollback per-rig? Adds complexity but de-risks.

## What I want from this review

Confirm:
- Is the A3 precedence inversion safe for trackers that have NOT set explicit name mappings?
- Does A4's `RemoteAwareUpdater` pattern match the existing tracker plumbing convention in the codebase (or is there a more idiomatic way)?
- Are A1–A2 sufficient or does `deferred` have other code paths I'm missing?
- Is the force-fetch in A4 actually a one-extra-API-call addition, or does it amplify worse for bulk syncs?
- Does B's validator extension have an existing place to live, or am I inventing the wrong abstraction?
- Is C's dry-run change going to add unacceptable latency to dry-runs in a 700-issue rig?
- Anything else broken or missing?

title: bug(linear): dry-run sync writes linear_issue_snapshots baseline rows — violates read-only contract
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Repro

bd 1.0.2 (ba642aab8) on houmanoids_www, fresh rig with empty linear_issue_snapshots table:

```
bd linear sync --pull --push --dry-run
  first sync — snapshotting baseline for issue hw-x6we (no conflict possible this run)
  first sync — snapshotting baseline for issue hw-kuswos (no conflict possible this run)
  ... (~200 more)
✓ Dry run complete (no changes made)
```

After: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM linear_issue_snapshots` → **207 rows**.

The dry-run claims 'no changes made' but the snapshot table was populated as a side effect.

## Why it matters

1. **Dry-run contract violation.** Users run --dry-run expecting zero DB side effects. The current behavior breaks that invariant. A user inspecting state after --dry-run gets different results than before.

2. **'First sync' state is consumable.** Running a dry-run consumes the soft-rollout grace period. The next wet-sync (which the user might have intended to be the 'real' first sync) finds the snapshots already populated and goes straight to field-scoped DetectConflicts. This means dry-run can change which code path wet-run takes — exactly the kind of differential the dry-run contract exists to prevent.

3. **Log line lies.** The output line is bare `first sync — snapshotting baseline for issue X (no conflict possible this run)` with no `[dry-run]` prefix, despite firing inside a --dry-run invocation. Either the prefix should be there (signaling 'would happen') OR the writer should be suppressed.

## Where it lives

bd-ajn's P3 snapshot writer in the pull-side path (PostPullSnapshotter capability hook) plus the first-encounter baseline writer in DetectConflicts. Neither is gated on dryRun.

Same likely true for bd-6cl's pull-side Project baseline writer — file separately if it has the same bug, or fold into this fix.

## Fix

Gate snapshot writes on dryRun across:
- Issue baseline writers (bd-ajn first-encounter path)
- Project baseline writers (bd-6cl PullProjects first-encounter path)
- The push-side post-mutation snapshot updates (bd-ajn P3 writers wrapping CreateIssue/UpdateIssue/AssignIssueToProject/SetIssueParent) — these only run after successful Linear mutations, so they're effectively dry-run-safe already; verify.

In dry-run mode, log lines should be prefixed: `[dry-run] Would snapshot baseline for issue X`. Same format pattern as other dry-run lines.

## Tests

- TestPullSync_DryRunDoesNotWriteSnapshots — assert snapshot count unchanged across dry-run
- TestFieldScopedSync_DryRunPreservesFirstSyncState — assert that running --dry-run before a wet-run does NOT consume the soft-rollout (wet-run still sees first-sync state)
- Extend existing dry-run tests if any exist with snapshot-count invariants

## Severity

P2: cosmetic-ish — the snapshot data itself is harmless (dolt-ignored local-only), and the dry-run still doesn't push/pull to Linear. But the differential-between-dry-and-wet behavior is real and reproducible. Worth fixing before bd-ajn's design is considered stable.

## How discovered

After bd-0iv landed, ran two dry-runs in sequence on houmanoids_www:
- First dry-run: ~207 'first sync — snapshotting baseline' lines fired
- Second dry-run: 0 such lines (the table now had rows)
- Query confirmed linear_issue_snapshots had 207 rows

Differential between consecutive dry-runs = dry-run isn't idempotent = dry-run is writing state.

## Follow-up to bd-1ay

bd-1ay (engine-wired ProjectSyncer) implements the **push** side: new top-level epics auto-create as Linear Projects, descendants get projectId via a post-sync reconcile pass.

This bead covers the **pull** side: Linear Projects discovered during pull get materialized as local epics in bd.

## Scope

1. **FetchProjects integration in doPull.** At the start of doPull (when tracker implements ProjectSyncer), call FetchProjects. For each Project:
   - Match by external_ref (Project URL) against local issues
   - If matched local epic → UPDATE bead.Title, bead.Description (split content/description), bead.Status (via reverse of MapEpicToProjectState)
   - If no match → CREATE new local epic (TypeEpic) with external_ref = Project URL
   - Description: Project.content if present, else Project.description (reverses the push-side split — bd-cs1)

2. **Descendant projectId → parent-child dep wiring.** When pulling an Issue with projectId set, walk to find the local epic whose external_ref matches that Project URL. Wire a parent-child dep from the Issue's bead to the epic's bead, idempotent (no-op if dep already exists).

3. **Tests:**
   - Pull-side FetchProjects → materialize Project as new local epic
   - Pull-side FetchProjects → update existing local epic from Project changes
   - Pull-side Issue with projectId → wires parent-child dep to local epic
   - Round-trip: push new epic → pull it back → identical local state

## Why follow-up not in bd-1ay

Push-side covers the primary use case: mayor/crew create epics in bd, push to Linear. Pull-side handles the inverse (someone creates a Project on Linear UI, bd discovers it on next sync) — important but secondary. Pearl flagged in her bd-1ay scope check that the pull-side has different risk profile: epic ID matching, descendant rewiring, bigger PR surface. Split per pearl's recommendation.

Not a quick-fix split — bd-1ay is structurally complete for what it does (push direction). This bead is a separate vertical (pull direction).

## Acceptance

- 'bd linear sync --pull' on a rig with new Linear Projects created via UI materializes them as local epics with correct content/description split
- Descendant Issues' projectId becomes a parent-child dep on the local epic
- 'bd linear sync --push --pull' on the same rig is a no-op after the first sync (idempotency)
- Existing FetchIssues path still handles regular Issues (not just Project-membered ones)

title: bug(linear): post-migration AssignIssueToProject bumps updatedAt, overrides local status changes on next pull
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Symptom

After running bd linear migrate-epic-to-project hw-sv1v on houmanoids_www (commit b3a05210d), the AssignIssueToProject call on each of 61 descendants bumped Linear's updatedAt to post-migration time. The user had 7 local 'closed' status changes from earlier (~May 22) that were still pending push. Next sync (bd linear sync --pull --push) ran pull first, saw Linear's updatedAt > local's, and imported Linear's 'Todo' status over the local 'closed' — reverting the 7 closes.

## Repro

1. Locally close some descendants of a migration target (status=closed)
2. Skip the immediate push so the changes are still local-only
3. Run migrate-epic-to-project on the parent epic (projectId-only mutation on each descendant via AssignIssueToProject)
4. Run 'bd linear sync --pull --push' immediately after
5. Local closes get reverted — Linear's stale 'Todo' wins because Linear.updatedAt > local.updatedAt

## Recovery (current workaround)

Reclose locally + 'bd linear push <ids>' bypasses the conflict gate via the force path. Works but manual.

## Root cause

Conflict resolution is whole-issue, timestamp-only. A content-only field mutation (projectId, content, etc.) shouldn't be able to outrank an unrelated semantic field mutation (status). The current 'newer timestamp wins' policy treats all updates as equivalent.

## Fix options

1. **Field-scoped conflict resolution**. Track per-field updatedAt or use a Set of dirty fields per side; merge non-conflicting fields, fall back to timestamp only for the truly-conflicting subset. Larger refactor.

2. **Migration tool issues local-side timestamp bumps too**. After AssignIssueToProject, call store.UpdateIssue with a marker that bumps the bead's updatedAt to match. Crude but simple.

3. **Migration tool's API calls use a no-bump endpoint or include a 'silent' flag if Linear supports it**. Not sure if Linear's GraphQL has this.

4. **Pre-flight check before migration**: detect pending local pushes on descendants and refuse/warn ('you have local changes on N descendants that aren't pushed; push them first to avoid override'). Smallest, least invasive.

I'd lean toward option 4 (pre-flight + warn) for v1 and option 1 (field-scoped) as the proper long-term fix.

## Not blocking

bd-go9/bd-cs1 are complete. Migration works. This is a corner case that bites only when local changes happen between sync and migration. Workaround exists.

## Provenance

Discovered by mayor while verifying bd-go9 wet-run on hw-sv1v (mail thread hq-wisp-fmrqd). bd 1.0.2 (b3a05210d).
notes:
Mayor decision 2026-06-08: pursue option 1 (field-scoped conflict resolution) as the canonical fix. Do not ship option 4 (plan-time pre-flight) as a separate v1 — that's a quick fix and we want the long-term correct solution.

Option 1 scope reminder from your filing:
- Replace whole-issue timestamp comparison with per-field tracking
- Each field carries its own last-modified timestamp (or equivalent — e.g. snapshot at last sync)
- Conflict resolver compares field-by-field; only fields where BOTH sides moved register as conflicts
- A pure projectId-set (e.g. from migration) doesn't override an unrelated status change

title: feat(linear): wire ProjectSyncer into engine — new top-level epics auto-create Linear Projects on push
description:
## Follow-up to bd-go9

bd-go9 (epic-identity migration tool) handles the LEGACY case: top-level epics that already exist as Issues get migrated to Projects via a user-initiated CLI.

This bead handles the FORWARD case: new top-level epics created locally should auto-sync as Projects on first push, not as Issues. Per the original epics-as-projects design intent.

## Current state

Per pearl's audit on feat/linear-epic-parent-child + integration sibling:

- `ProjectSyncer` interface defined in `internal/tracker/tracker.go`
- Linear adapter implements all methods in `internal/linear/tracker.go` (CreateProject, UpdateProject, FetchProjects, AssignIssueToProject, SetIssueParent, IsProjectRef, ExtractProjectID)
- BUT: zero callers anywhere outside the adapter itself. No `doEpicSync`, no `epicProjectMap`, no epic-skip in `doPush`. The engine never invokes any of it.

Result: every top-level epic created today gets pushed as an Issue. hw-sv1v wasn't pre-design legacy; that's just current behavior.

## Scope

Wire the engine to use ProjectSyncer when the tracker implements it:

1. **doEpicSync** pass in the push pipeline. For each top-level epic (no parent-epic dep) with no external_ref OR with a Project-URL external_ref, call `CreateProject` / `UpdateProject`. Track results in an `epicProjectMap` keyed by bead ID → Linear project ID.

2. **doPush epic-skip.** Skip pushing top-level epics that were synced via doEpicSync (present in epicProjectMap) so they don't double-create as Issues.

3. **doPush descendant projectId.** For non-epic descendants whose nearest top-level-epic ancestor is in epicProjectMap, call `AssignIssueToProject` on the Linear Issue after create/update.

4. **Pull side.** When FetchProjects returns Projects, materialize them as local epics (TypeEpic) with external_ref = Project URL. Existing FetchIssues continues handling regular Issues.

5. **Reconciler awareness** (interplay with bd-9w3 + bd-go9): if child's bead-parent has external_ref pointing to a Project URL (`IsProjectRef`), the parent reconciler should set `projectId` on the child, NOT `parentId` (which would fail/error because Project IDs aren't valid Issue parent IDs).

## Out of scope for v1

- Project state mapping refinements beyond MapEpicToProjectState
- Cross-team project assignment heuristics
- Project archival on epic close (probably should — Linear projects have a 'completed' state)
- Bidirectional updates if a user manually changes Project metadata on Linear (FetchProjects pull-side covers basic title/desc/state; complex metadata round-trip can land later)

## Why P2 not P1

- bd-go9 plus its --legacy-issue=keep default gives mayor a complete workflow for the immediate hw-sv1v case
- New epics can still be migrated post-creation with the bd-go9 tool until this lands
- Higher-risk change (touches push engine, which has been the most-burnt area: bd-47l, bd-joz, bd-ena, bd-9w3); deserves separate care
- Pearl explicitly flagged this as the larger 'Path B' option in her bd-go9 scope check; mayor agreed to defer

Captured as a follow-up so it doesn't get lost.

title: feat(linear): add dry-run preview to bd-ena parent reconciler
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Problem

The bd-ena parent-child reconciler can't be previewed. `internal/linear/parent_reconcile.go:118` defines `ReconcileParents(ctx, links)` with no dry-run param — every call mutates Linear via `childE.client.UpdateIssue(...)`. Because of that, the caller in `cmd/bd/linear.go:352` is forced to gate on `!dryRun`:

```go
if push && !dryRun && result.Success && !syncIsScoped(&opts) {
    reconcileLinearParents(ctx, lt, &result.Warnings)
}
```

So `bd linear sync --pull --push --dry-run` can verify the rest of the sync is clean, but tells us NOTHING about what the parent reconciler would do. For the HOU-164..209 orphan-repair use case this defeats the whole point of a dry-run pre-flight before a wet sync — exactly the situation the cancel-cascade incident taught us to never do again.

## Fix

1. `ReconcileParents(ctx, links, dryRun bool)` — when `dryRun`, the `if Parent.ID != desired` branch skips the `UpdateIssue` call but still appends to `stats.Updated` (or a new `stats.WouldUpdate` for clarity). The read-only fetches still run so idempotency / NotFound / parent-lookup behavior is exercised.
2. Drop the `!dryRun` gate at `cmd/bd/linear.go:352` — pass `dryRun` through to `reconcileLinearParents`, which forwards to `ReconcileParents`.
3. In `reconcileLinearParents`, when called in dry-run, print:
   - `[dry-run] Would reconcile N parent link(s)` summary
   - one `[dry-run] Would set parent of CHILD → PARENT` line per link that would mutate
   - skipped/notfound counts in the existing channel
4. Add a test mirroring the existing `reconcile_test.go` cases with `dryRun: true` asserting no `UpdateIssue` calls but correct `WouldUpdate` counts. The mockLinearServer already tracks update calls.

## Why now

Mayor just rebuilt gt to fix a separate reaper regression (PATH binary was built from cog's branch, missing the external_ref filter — that's why HOU-164..209 kept getting reaper-closed despite the May 12 'fix'). Reopened 23 external_ref beads. Dry-run is now clean on the surrounding sync, but we can't dry-run the parent reconcile itself, so we're either flying blind into a wet sync or skipping the feature verification.

## Acceptance

- `bd linear sync --pull --push --dry-run` on houmanoids_www prints per-link `[dry-run] Would set parent` lines for HOU-164..209 (and skip lines for any whose Linear parent already matches).
- No `UpdateIssue` mutations issued during dry-run (verifiable via mock).
- Cherry-picks cleanly onto `feat/linear-epic-parent-child-integrated` (mayor's local testing sibling) AND onto the upstream PR branch `feat/linear-epic-parent-child".
- Reconciler still skipped on scoped syncs (`--parent` / `--issues`) in both wet and dry modes — that logic at `syncIsScoped` stays.

## Branching

Add as a new commit on `feat/linear-epic-parent-child` (the upstream PR branch, not the integration sibling). Then rebuild the integration sibling on top via mayor's bd-rebuild-integrated.sh so we get a binary to rerun the dry-run.

description:

## Symptom

After a wet sync that pushed a fresh epic tree (\`hw-sv1v\` teleop-video-livekit, with 9 phase sub-epics and ~46 task children) to Linear, the parent epic + sub-epics were created as separate flat issues with no parent-child relationship set on the Linear side.

Concretely (on the houmanoids_www rig, 2026-05-12):

- Top-level epic locally: \`hw-sv1v\` (issue_type=epic) → pushed as HOU-159, **parent=null**
- Sub-epic locally: \`hw-sv1v.1\` (issue_type=epic) → pushed as HOU-158, **parent=null** (expected: parent=HOU-159)
- Phase 1 task children: \`hw-sv1v.1.1\` through \`hw-sv1v.1.7\` → HOU-151..157, **parent=null** (expected: parent=HOU-158)
- Subsequent phase tasks: HOU-164 through HOU-209 (~46 issues), **all parent=null** (expected: parent=their respective Phase epic)

Live snapshot of the orphan state on Linear: https://linear.app/houmanoids/team/HOU/all (filter to HOU-164..209)

The beads tree IS correctly structured locally — \`bd show hw-sv1v\` reflects the parent-child hierarchy, and the dependency type is \`parent-child\` on each row. Confirmed via:

  bd list --json --status all --limit 200 | jq -r '.[] | select(.id | startswith("hw-sv1v")) | .id + " | " + .issue_type + " | parent=" + (.parent_issue_id // "none")'

## Expected behavior

\`bd linear sync\` should push the bead's parent-child structure to Linear's parent issue field, so:
1. Sub-epics under a top-level epic have parent=<top-level-epic-linear-id>
2. Task children under a sub-epic have parent=<sub-epic-linear-id>

This is supposed to work (per the user's expectation that "beads-linear sync is supposed to create epics correctly"). Either the feature exists but is silently failing, or the implementation never landed for the Linear adapter.

## What to investigate

1. **Is parent-child push implemented for the Linear adapter?** Check \`internal/linear/tracker.go::CreateIssue\` and \`UpdateIssue\` — do they pass parent on the IssueCreate/IssueUpdate mutations? Linear's GraphQL schema has \`IssueCreateInput.parentId\` and \`IssueUpdateInput.parentId\`.
2. **If yes**, why is it not firing? Likely candidates:
   - Sync order: children get pushed before parents, so parent has no external_ref yet at push time. Need a topological order, or a two-pass: create all issues first, then reconcile parent links.
   - Field mapper drops parent: check \`internal/linear/mapping.go::IssueToTracker\` — does it set parent_id when source local issue has a parent dependency?
3. **If no**, scope the work: add the parent push, plus a backfill mode that reconciles parent links for already-pushed beads (for HOU-164..209 we'll want to repair, not re-create).

## Repair path for the existing orphan state

Pearl probably can ship as one PR: implement parent-child push + add a one-shot \`bd linear repair-parents\` (or just rely on the next sync after the fix lands) to wire up the existing 46+ orphan issues using their existing external_refs.

- [ ] New epic creation in a fresh tree (e.g. test with a 3-level toy epic) produces correctly-linked Linear issues in one sync.
- [ ] No re-creation of existing issues — repair must match by \`external_ref\` and only set the missing parent field.

Codex-Reviewed-By trailer before push; tests for the topo-order / two-pass logic.

title: Implement linear.exclude_id_prefix and linear.exclude_id_patterns config keys
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Problem

The houmanoids_www rig config has these keys set:
```
linear.exclude_id_prefix = hw-mol-
linear.exclude_id_patterns = mol-
```
…but bd doesn't read either of them. The keys were set with the intent to exclude workflow-artifact beads (gt-toolkit pipeline molecules: "Brainstorming dialogue", "Opus 4.6: Consolidate", etc.) from being pushed/created in Linear, but the filtering code doesn't exist in `internal/linear/` or `cmd/bd/linear.go`.

Result: 25 `hw-mol-*` beads are flagged as "Would create in Linear" on every dry-run, polluting Linear with workflow internals.

The existing `linear.exclude_types = molecule,event` filter handles type-based exclusion correctly, but many of these `hw-mol-*` beads are typed `task` rather than `molecule`, so type-based exclusion misses them. The ID prefix is the only reliable identifier.

## Prior art

`ready.exclude_id_patterns` already exists upstream (e.g. `upstream/feat/label-pattern-matching`, `internal/storage/sqlite/ready.go:891` defines `ExcludeIDPatternsConfigKey = "ready.exclude_id_patterns"`). It filters `bd ready` work selection. Mirror that semantics for linear sync push.

## What

Implement two new config keys in the linear push path:

### `linear.exclude_id_prefix`

Single string. Beads whose ID starts with this prefix are excluded from push (both create and update). Comparison is case-sensitive on the full bead ID (e.g. `hw-mol-`).

### `linear.exclude_id_patterns`

Comma-separated list of substrings. Beads whose ID contains ANY of these substrings (case-sensitive, anywhere in the ID) are excluded from push. Default: empty (no patterns).

Examples:
```
bd config set linear.exclude_id_prefix "hw-mol-"
bd config set linear.exclude_id_patterns "-wisp-,sandbox-,scratch-"
```

If both keys are set, exclusion is the union (matches either rule → excluded).

## Where the filter applies

PUSH direction only:
- `bd linear sync` (--push or bidirectional)
- The exclusion fires BEFORE the create-or-update decision, mirroring how `linear.exclude_types` and `linear.exclude_labels` are applied today (search for those in `cmd/bd/linear.go` for the call site).

PULL direction is unaffected (pull is gated by `external_ref` already; no local-ID filter needed).

## Behavior on already-synced beads

A bead that previously synced to Linear (has `external_ref`) but now matches an exclude rule:
- The Linear issue is left alone (NOT deleted, NOT archived).
- Future updates from this bead are silently skipped (no push).
- Document this in the config-set help text — users who add an exclude rule for already-synced beads should manually archive/delete those Linear issues if desired.

## Tests

- `TestLinearSync_ExcludeIDPrefix`: with `linear.exclude_id_prefix = hw-mol-`, a `hw-mol-foo` bead is skipped from push (no create, no update); a `hw-foo` bead is pushed normally.
- `TestLinearSync_ExcludeIDPatterns`: with `linear.exclude_id_patterns = mol-,wisp-`, beads with `mol-` or `wisp-` anywhere in the ID are skipped; others push.
- `TestLinearSync_ExcludeIDBoth`: both keys, union semantics.
- `TestLinearSync_ExcludeID_AlreadySynced`: a bead with `external_ref` that NOW matches an exclude rule produces no API call (verify via mock); the Linear-side issue persists.
- `TestLinearSync_DryRunRespectsExcludeID`: `bd linear sync --dry-run` does NOT print "Would create" or "Would push" for excluded beads.

## Files likely touched

- `cmd/bd/linear.go` — read the new config keys; pass to the engine or fieldmapper as a filter predicate.
- `internal/linear/tracker.go` or `internal/tracker/engine.go` — apply the filter in `collectBatchPushIssues` and the per-issue push loop alongside existing `exclude_types` / `exclude_labels` filters.
- Test files under `cmd/bd/` and `internal/linear/`.

## Acceptance

After this lands and the houmanoids_www rig syncs:
- `bd linear sync --dry-run` produces 0 "Would create in Linear" lines for `hw-mol-*` beads.
- Existing `Robot SIM card registration` and `Drizzle migrations` real beads (typed `feature`) still appear as "Would create".
- The codex review gate is run on this PR before merge.

## Not in scope

- Adding pattern-matching beyond literal substring (no regex). Mirror `ready.exclude_id_patterns` semantics — substring is enough.
- Changing the data layer or migrating existing `hw-mol-*` beads' types.
- Per-team / per-project overrides (single global key per rig is fine).

title: Tighten NormalizeLinearMarkdown: bullet style and tilde escape drift causes spurious push loop
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Problem

After deploying the bd-47l A-C patches and running a clean dry-run on the houmanoids_www rig (with the new state_map config in place), 30 beads continuously classify as "Would push field change (state preserved)". `--verbose-diff` shows ZERO diff lines for any of them — only the 3 legitimate state-change beads get diff annotations.

A wet sync would push bd's description for each, Linear would re-normalize on store, the next sync would see the same drift again and want to push again. Infinite loop of no-op API calls.

## Reproduction

On the houmanoids_www rig with bd commit 0d4a249c installed:

```bash
cd ~/gt/houmanoids_www/mayor/rig
bd linear sync --dry-run --verbose-diff 2>&1 | grep -c "field change (state preserved)"  # 30
bd linear sync --dry-run --verbose-diff 2>&1 | grep -c "·"                                # only 3 (state-only)
```

Pick any of the 30 (e.g. `hw-bwka` / HOU-88) and diff the raw descriptions:

```bash
cd ~/gt/houmanoids_www/mayor/rig
bd list --json --status all --limit 1000 | jq -r '.[] | select(.id == "hw-bwka") | .description' > /tmp/local-desc.txt
curl -s -X POST https://api.linear.app/graphql -H "Authorization: $LINEAR_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"query { issues(filter: {team: {id: {eq: \"97cacca1-802b-484a-97e4-5948aeebfc2b\"}}, number: {eq: 88}}, first: 1) { nodes { description } } }"}' \
  | jq -r '.data.issues.nodes[0].description' > /tmp/linear-desc.txt
diff /tmp/local-desc.txt /tmp/linear-desc.txt
```

## Drift patterns observed

Two patterns account for all the diffs across the 30 affected beads:

1. **Bullet markers**: bd stores `- item`, Linear stores `* item` after rendering. Same content semantically but byte-different.
2. **Tilde escape**: bd stores plain `~` (e.g. `(~line 60-74)`), Linear stores `\~` after rendering.
3. (Possibly): trailing blank lines between sections appear/disappear.

Sample diff snippet from hw-bwka:

```
< - Send ModeCommand with action="motion_state" to switch robot from RL (17) → Stand (1)
< - Now Z/Roll/Pitch commands ...
---
> * Send ModeCommand with action="motion_state" to switch robot from RL (17) → Stand (1)
> * Now Z/Roll/Pitch commands ...

< app/houdini/lib/robotCommunication/MovementController.ts — posture mode toggle lives here (~line 60-74).
---
> app/houdini/lib/robotCommunication/MovementController.ts — posture mode toggle lives here (\~line 60-74).
```

## Diagnosis

The internal disagreement is between two equality paths that *should* agree:

- `PushFieldsEqual` (mapping.go:663) — uses `NormalizeLinearMarkdown` on both sides. Returns FALSE for these 30 (per ContentEqual returning false in cmd/bd/linear.go:530+).
- `PushFieldsDiff` (mapping.go:697) — uses the SAME `NormalizeLinearMarkdown`. Returns empty diff slice (verbose-diff prints nothing).

Both call `NormalizeLinearMarkdown(BuildLinearDescription(local)) ?? NormalizeLinearMarkdown(remote.Description)` — same inputs, same function, but *one* returns "different" and the other returns "no diffs". Either:

- `NormalizeLinearMarkdown` is non-deterministic (unlikely)
- `PushFieldsEqual`'s comparison is correctly catching the drift but `PushFieldsDiff`'s description-diff branch is filtering it out somewhere (e.g. zero-length result from describeNormalizedTextDiff, or an intermediate `if normalizedLocal != normalizedRemote` evaluation differing across calls)
- Some other field is the actual disagreement source — needs a printf-style trace

## Acceptance criteria

After this fix, on the houmanoids_www rig with no other changes:

1. `bd linear sync --dry-run` should report 0 "Would push field change (state preserved)" entries (only legitimate field/state changes remain).
2. If any "field change" remains, `--verbose-diff` MUST surface the diff that triggered ContentEqual=false. PushFieldsEqual and PushFieldsDiff must agree.
3. A wet sync followed immediately by another dry-run should produce ZERO new pushes — the post-sync state must converge, no perpetual drift loop.
4. Existing tests still pass; add regression test for `-`/`*` bullet drift and `~`/`\~` tilde escape (real samples from hw-bwka work fine as fixtures).

## Hints / starting points

- `NormalizeLinearMarkdown` is at `internal/linear/mapping.go:64`.
- Existing normalizer fixes from this branch handle: `__bold__` underscores, bracket escapes, escaped quotes, Linear-side leading indent, case-insensitive labels. Bullet `-`/`*` and tilde escape are uncovered.
- Markdown spec says `-`, `*`, and `+` are equivalent unordered-list markers — normalizer should canonicalize to one form before compare.
- Tilde escape: Linear's renderer escapes `~` because GFM uses `~~strikethrough~~`. A single `~` in the middle of text gets escaped to `\~` on round-trip. Normalizer should strip the backslash before `~` (and probably similar safe-escape forms).

## Out of scope

- Don't touch the state-preservation logic (A4 in bd-47l). That's working correctly and the 3 state-change items in current dry-run are accurate.
- Don't touch label sync. Label diff is already correctly surfaced when present.

## Provenance

- Discovered during F-verification of bd-47l on houmanoids_www rig (Mayor session, 2026-05-03).
- Blocking: would force F4 verification (title-edit roundtrip) to be unreliable because spurious description churn drowns out the signal.
- bd binary in use: 1.0.2 (commit 4d35e481 / 0d4a249c).
close_reason: Shipped 4 commits (db352059, 18d7fb49, da2d9010, b02f3ce3). Mayor verified on houmanoids_www rig: 30 spurious 'Would push field change (state preserved)' beads → 0. Per-iteration catch: defense-in-depth normalizer (4), hasLabelDelta error-path symmetry (0), forced-path ContentEqual gate (25 — the real win), in-shield escape strip (1). Final state: 0 spurious, 3 legitimate state changes, 11 legitimate pull-updates, 1 new bead create. bd-47l F-verification blocker lifted.

title: linear: case-insensitive matching in reconciler truth table (v2 case-sensitivity)
description:
The reconciler matches label names case-sensitively in pass 3 (the truth table). Mismatched casing between bead and Linear (e.g. bead has "bug", Linear has "Bug") manifests as a thrash:
- Pass 3 sees "bug" as bead-only → AddToLinear=["bug"]
- Pass 3 sees "Bug" as linear-only → AddToBeads=["Bug"]
- LabelsByName resolves "bug" case-insensitively to existing "Bug" id → push dedup yields no-op labelIds
- Pull adds "Bug" to bead → bead now has [bug, Bug] (data duplication)
- Each subsequent sync repeats the dance

Documented as a known limitation in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-linear-label-sync-design.md (Self-Review section). Round 3-5 codex passes addressed the dangerous failure modes (no infinite churn, no silent data loss, no PK violations on snapshot insert), but the underlying case-sensitive matching was deferred to v2.

Verified in production by mayor on houmanoids_www / hw-gxrq:
  · labels +[bug] (push to Linear)
  · labels -[Bug] (remove from Linear)

Fix: case-fold all name matching in the reconciler's classifyRenames + applyTruthTable. Preserve original case for outputs (snapshot keeps Linear's display case via existing logic). May also want a one-shot "label case normalization" migration to align existing beads with their Linear counterparts on first sync after the v2 fix.

Add comment and attachment sync to the bd Linear integration.

## Requirements
1. **Bidirectional comment sync**: Comments in beads ↔ Linear. Match by external_ref to avoid duplicates.
2. **Attachment pull**: Pull attachment metadata from Linear → beads (pull-only). Store URL/metadata, not file content.
3. **Incremental**: Only sync changes since last sync timestamp.
4. **Non-breaking**: Use optional interfaces (CommentSyncer, AttachmentFetcher) so Jira/ADO/GitHub/GitLab adapters don't need changes.

## Implementation Plan (execute in order)

### Phase 1: Schema & Types
1. Schema migration: add external_ref VARCHAR(255) and updated_at DATETIME to comments table (and wisp_comments). Add index on external_ref.
2. Schema migration: create attachments table (id, issue_id, external_ref, filename, url, mime_type, size_bytes, source, creator, created_at). FK to issues.
3. Update types.Comment to add ExternalRef and UpdatedAt fields. Create new types.Attachment struct.

### Phase 2: Storage Layer  
4. Add storage methods: GetCommentByExternalRef, ImportIssueCommentWithRef, UpdateCommentExternalRef. Update existing comment queries to include new columns.
5. Add attachment CRUD: CreateAttachment, GetIssueAttachments, GetAttachmentByExternalRef.

### Phase 3: Tracker Framework
6. Define optional interfaces in tracker/tracker.go:
   - CommentSyncer: FetchComments(ctx, externalIssueID, since) and CreateComment(ctx, externalIssueID, body)
   - AttachmentFetcher: FetchAttachments(ctx, externalIssueID)
   Add TrackerComment and TrackerAttachment types.

### Phase 4: Linear Client
7. Add GraphQL queries/mutations to linear/client.go:
   - FetchIssueComments(ctx, issueID, since) — paginated query on issue.comments
   - CreateComment(ctx, issueID, body) — commentCreate mutation  
   - FetchIssueAttachments(ctx, issueID) — paginated query on issue.attachments
8. Implement CommentSyncer and AttachmentFetcher on linear.Tracker.

### Phase 5: Sync Engine
9. Add comment sync phase to engine.go after issue push:
   - Pull: For issues with external_ref, fetch remote comments, create locally if external_ref not found
   - Push: For local comments without external_ref, create in Linear, store returned ID
10. Add attachment pull phase: fetch and store attachment metadata for issues with external_ref.

### Phase 6: CLI & Polish
11. Add flags to cmd/bd/linear.go: --no-comments, --no-attachments, --comments-only
12. Update output to show comment/attachment stats.
13. Update examples/linear-workflow/README.md to document the feature.

## Key Design Decisions
- Optional interfaces (not modifying IssueTracker) to avoid breaking other adapters
- Comment edit sync deferred to follow-up (just skip existing by external_ref for now)
- Attachments are metadata-only (URL, filename, size) — no file downloads
- Separate last_comment_sync / last_attachment_sync config keys
